baselineFields.Subjective: The patient reports experiencing dizziness that began twelve days ago. The dizziness occurs when standing up quickly, lasts about thirty seconds per episode, and is described as mild (previously described as severe, but corrected to mild). The patient has not fainted and is able to walk and carry out normal routines. There were two episodes of dizziness yesterday (corrected from an earlier count of seven). The patient drinks about four glasses of water daily. The patient had a mild headache yesterday but does not have one today. The patient has not started, stopped, or changed any medications. The patient's home blood pressure reading was 118/72 (corrected from an earlier misstatement of 180/72).
baselineFields.Objective: No physical examination findings or vital signs were provided during this encounter. The only objective data is the patient's home blood pressure reading of 118/72.
baselineFields.Assessment: Orthostatic dizziness, mild, with onset twelve days ago, triggered by standing quickly. No associated syncope, chest pain, shortness of breath, or current headache. The symptoms are mild and do not interfere with daily activities. No medication changes or new medications reported. Home blood pressure is within normal limits. The likely etiology is benign orthostatic dizziness, possibly related to mild dehydration or rapid postural changes.
baselineFields.Plan:
- Rise slowly from sitting or lying positions to reduce episodes of orthostatic dizziness.
- Maintain regular fluid intake to prevent dehydration and reduce dizziness.
- Keep a brief symptom diary, recording when dizziness occurs and how long it lasts, to monitor frequency and duration of episodes.
- Use the corrected episode count (two episodes yesterday) and duration (thirty seconds) in the diary for accurate tracking.
- No new medications will be started, as symptoms are mild and manageable with conservative measures.
- Schedule a follow-up appointment in 10 days to reassess dizziness and review the symptom diary.
